subject: Discovery recap: latency & concurrency targets (DataCo)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@dataco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Intro — system scaling discussion / Neha recap

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the concrete asks so we can align internal teams:

Pain points (as described):
- Streaming UX: your product shows perceptible lag for live transcription and real-time assistant flows — end-users report jitter when multiple agents are active.
- Latency spikes: p95 for streaming responses currently ~420–500 ms depending on load; target is p95 <= 200 ms for interactive flows.
- Concurrency limits: spikes when more than ~40 concurrent websocket streams hit the service; backend queues and tokenization step are bottlenecks.
- Cost predictability: bursty workload causes cost spikes; you want predictable unit economics for peak demo days.

Current stack & constraints:
- Models: a mix of a proprietary LLM (on-prem) for sensitive prompts + open LLMs on AWS for general assistance.
- Inference: hosted on AWS Fargate doing containerized inference proxy; fronted by API gateway and websocket layer.
- Typical payloads: average 60 tokens output per response, peaks to 400 tokens; median sequence length ~80 tokens.
- Compliance: must route sensitive traffic through your on-prem model; otherwise open-model traffic is fine in cloud.

Success criteria for POC:
1) p95 streaming latency <= 200 ms for median payloads at 50 concurrent streams.
2) Sustain 800 requests/sec for batched embedding jobs with <500 ms p95.
3) No sensitive data leaves your on-prem boundary (we can support hybrid routing).
4) Operational visibility: per-route latency and token-level cost breakdown in Redwood Console.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- Rishi to run a short sizing exercise against a representative trace you shared (attach: dataco_latency_samples.csv).
- 2-week Dedicated POC: reserved GPU pool to validate p95 targets with real traffic.
- Canary routing plan: start with 10% traffic, auto-fallback to current infra.
- Procurement: please intro procurement@dataco.com for contract/PO timelines.

Attachments:
- dataco_latency_samples.csv (csv)
- shared doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExample (POC checklist)

If this looks right I can coordinate times for a technical deep-dive with Rishi + a calendar for the POC kickoff next week.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Neha,

Thanks — accurate summary. A few clarifications:
- Our p95 numbers are end-to-end (client -> app -> model -> client). The backend inference portion is roughly 250–300 ms of that today.
- Peak concurrent streams we care about for this POC are 60 (we run occasional 100+ for demos).
- Payload note: many responses are multi-turn; average 60 tokens is correct but 90 tokens is realistic.

Procurement contact is procurement@dataco.com — they can handle the MSA/PO.
SOC 2: we will need SOC 2 type II or equivalent evidence for any cloud-hosted work; happy to talk private deployment options.

Emily

Subject: Re: Intro — system scaling discussion / Neha recap

Emily / Neha,

Quick technical notes after looking at dataco_latency_samples.csv and the trace snippets:
- Tokenization overhead: for multi-turn flows we see ~30–40 ms per request for tokenization at your payload sizes; we can offload to a dedicated tokenizer process to save ~20–25 ms.
- KV cache reuse: enabling aggressive prefix caching for repeated system prompts should drop p95 in practice; need a stable keying strategy.
- Batching: for embedding workloads we recommend a micro-batching window of 10–20 ms to optimize throughput without hurting interactive latency.

Provisional sizing (very conservative):
- For streaming interactive flows with target p95 200 ms at 60 concurrent streams: 2 x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (quantized model runtime), continuous batching disabled for the interactive path.
- For embeddings at 800 RPS target: 1 x A100-equivalent with batching policy tuned as above (batch size ~64 depending on tokenization).

I've attached a quick modeling workbook and a PoC run template to make the rough numbers reproducible on your side.

Attachments:
- redwood_latency_modeling.xlsx (xlsx)
- poc_run_template.yaml (yaml)

Happy to run through the workbook live — propose a 45-min deep-dive Tue/Wed this week.

—Rishi
